mill-a.prompt: CAMERA, STYLE AND SCALE REFERENCES: the first attached panel is this game's GENERAL STORE, a four-tile-wide building, drawn in the game's camera (the front square to the viewer, the roof seen from above, the grid straight) and its painterly whimsical rendering with bright full daylight; match that camera, rendering and daylight exactly, and match its SCALE: this station is two tiles wide, so its posts and walls are about as tall as that store's door, people-sized, never a toy next to it. CONCEPT REFERENCE: the second attached image is this game's old MILL drawing in an earlier style: keep its LAYOUT (the millstone at the LEFT under the windmill blades, which are one machine; sacks of flour, a sack of sugar and a heap of grain at the RIGHT, a wooden scoop) and nothing of its rendering. SUBJECT: the MILL, one of this game's 2 x 2 CRAFTING STATIONS. Every crafting station shares ONE FRAMEWORK: an open-air cut-away workshop STALL, never a closed house: a back wall along the top edge, two short side walls coming forward from its ends, no front wall and no roof over the front, so the camera looks straight into the workshop; the floor packed earth with a few flagstones; the product being made stands big in the open front. Each station differs by its props, its silhouette and its accent colour. FRAMEWORK OPTION A, THATCH AND STONE: the back wall is cream plaster over a grey stone footing with honey timber framing, the side stubs are stone, and a narrow strip of golden THATCH with a wooden ridge beam sits along the top of the back wall like an awning; the windmill is a stout wooden post with four wheat-tan canvas sails rising from the left end of the back wall. THE WORK, drawn big and obvious in the open front so a player knows the station at a glance: a round grey MILLSTONE on a wooden frame at the left, driven by a small wooden WINDMILL whose four sails rise above the roof as the station's defining silhouette; at the right plump sacks of white flour, one tied sack of sugar and a golden heap of grain with a wooden scoop. ACCENT COLOUR: WHEAT TAN (the flour and grain), on the awning or roof and the sails.  The LAST attached image is a layout guide, a patch of the board grid with a tan 2 x 2 square: the station's walls and floor fill that 2 x 2 square entirely, back wall on its top edge, ground contact on its bottom edge, side walls to its left and right edges (the roof or awning and the windmill sails may rise above it), with a soft contact shadow to the lower right. Fill the surrounding squares with plain short grass in the same style, no props beyond those named, and draw the faint grid lines as thin tile edges. Do not leave the tan square tan. No letters anywhere, no people, no animals, no smoke.
